facts.fact: Adwave's vendor page says campaigns start at $30/day for its streaming TV advertising.
facts.quote: Campaigns start at just [$30/day](https://adwave.com/pricing), making TV accessible for any budget

facts.fact: Adwave's guide recommends $200-500 per month on streaming TV to build meaningful name recognition in a city council district.
facts.quote: Even $200-500 per month on streaming TV can build meaningful name recognition in a city council district.

facts.fact: The guide estimates direct mail costs $0.75-2.00 per piece including design, printing, and postage.
facts.quote: Expensive per piece ($0.75-2.00 including design, printing, postage)

facts.fact: The guide suggests planning for 3-5 mail pieces to the target voter list.
facts.quote: Plan for 3-5 mail pieces to your target voter list.

facts.fact: The guide estimates a city council race targeting 10,000 households might spend $7,500-15,000 on a full mail program.
facts.quote: A city council race targeting 10,000 households might spend $7,500-15,000 on a full mail program.

facts.fact: The guide recommends $500-2,000 per month for Facebook, Instagram, and Google ads for a local race.
facts.quote: **Budget guidance:** $500-2,000 per month for a local race, focusing on video content and voter engagement.

facts.fact: Per the guide citing the Knight Foundation, fewer than 30% of Americans can name their city council representative.
facts.quote: Research from the Knight Foundation shows that fewer than 30% of Americans can name their city council representative.

facts.fact: The guide states midterm local elections might see 15-25% turnout, and off-cycle elections can drop to single digits.
facts.quote: Midterm local elections might see 15-25% turnout, and off-cycle elections can drop to single digits.

facts.fact: Per the Analyst Institute, personal contact at the door has turnout effects of 4 to 9 percentage points.
facts.quote: Research from the Analyst Institute reports turnout effects of 4 to 9 percentage points for personal contact at the door.

facts.fact: Google restricts political ad targeting to geographic and age-based targeting only, according to the guide.
facts.quote: Google restricts political ad targeting to geographic and age-based only

facts.fact: Meta requires political ad authorization and disclaimers for political ads, according to the guide.
facts.quote: Meta requires political ad authorization and disclaimers

facts.fact: AdWave's guidance gives a budget of $200-1,000 for a series of print ads during the campaign window.
facts.quote: **Budget guidance:** $200-1,000 for a series of print ads during the campaign window.

facts.fact: The page recommends a total advertising budget of $3,000-15,000 for city council campaigns, depending on district size and competitiveness.
facts.quote: **Total budget range:** $3,000-15,000 depending on district size and competitiveness.

facts.fact: The page recommends streaming TV for city council campaigns at $300-1,000 per month for 2-3 months before the election.
facts.quote: Streaming TV** for name recognition across the district ($300-1,000/month for 2-3 months before election)

facts.fact: The page recommends at least 3 direct mail pieces for city council campaigns targeting high-propensity voters.
facts.quote: Direct mail** targeting high-propensity voters (3 pieces minimum)

facts.fact: The page states city council districts typically have populations ranging from 10,000 to 100,000+.
facts.quote: with populations ranging from 10,000 to 100,000+.

facts.fact: The page recommends a total advertising budget of $10,000-50,000 for county commission races, depending on county size.
facts.quote: **Total budget range:** $10,000-50,000 depending on county size.

facts.fact: The page recommends streaming TV as the primary awareness channel for county commission races at $500-2,000 per month for 3-4 months.
facts.quote: Streaming TV** as the primary awareness channel ($500-2,000/month for 3-4 months)

facts.fact: The page recommends 4-5 direct mail pieces to targeted voter segments for county commission races.
facts.quote: Direct mail** to targeted voter segments (4-5 pieces)

facts.fact: The page recommends a total advertising budget of $2,000-10,000 for school board races.
facts.quote: **Total budget range:** $2,000-10,000.

facts.fact: The page recommends streaming TV for school board races targeting households with school-age children at $200-750 per month.
facts.quote: Streaming TV** targeting households with school-age children ($200-750/month)

facts.fact: The page states AdWave campaigns start at $30 a day for streaming TV advertising.
facts.quote: With [campaigns starting at $30 a day](https://adwave.com/pricing) and geographic targeting

facts.fact: The page recommends starting name recognition advertising 3-4 months before election day.
facts.quote: Start name recognition efforts 3-4 months before election day.

facts.fact: The page recommends beginning policy-focused advertising 6-8 weeks before election day.
facts.quote: Begin policy-focused advertising 6-8 weeks out, and hit maximum intensity in the final 2-3 weeks.

facts.fact: The page recommends canvassing city council high-density areas during the final 6 weeks of the campaign.
facts.quote: **Canvassing** in high-density areas during the final 6 weeks

facts.fact: The page states that local races are governed by state election laws, while Federal Election Commission rules apply to federal races.
facts.quote: Federal Election Commission rules apply to federal races. Local races are governed by state election laws, which vary significantly.
